title: Anthropic prices its IPO tonight with the book six to seven times oversubscribed
subtitle: Underwriters are preparing to price above the $70–$78 range, setting up a Nasdaq debut Thursday under ticker ANT and a combined public-plus-private raise near $90 billion.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic prices its IPO the evening of November 18, 2026. The company is offering 825 million Class A shares and the original filed range is $70 to $78. Order books closed Tuesday oversubscribed six to seven times available shares, and underwriters are preparing to price above the top of the range, CNBC reported citing people familiar with the deal. Trading begins Thursday, November 19, on Nasdaq under ticker ANT. A parallel private placement of non-voting shares at the IPO price brings the combined raise to roughly $90.4 billion at the high end — above the $75 billion SpaceX raised in June, which would make this the largest offering on record.

The six-to-seven-times coverage is the detail that changes the story. A book that deep lets underwriters price above range without losing the aftermarket pop that institutional allocators want, which is why the pricing-above-78 signal matters more than any single valuation number. The private placement — Google is one of seven buyers taking non-voting shares at the IPO price — also lets strategic partners lock in exposure without voting rights, a structure that keeps Anthropic's board insulated from the kind of governance pressure that just took Jensen Huang out at NVIDIA.

This caps a pricing week that started with NVIDIA's blowout Q3 on Monday and OpenAI's GPT-6.2 launch on Tuesday. The three events together form the capital-market test of the AI cycle: the infrastructure vendor delivered, the frontier lab shipped the next model, and the pure-play safety-first lab is testing whether the public market will pay the valuation the private market has been assigning for two years. If ANT opens green Thursday, the window stays open for OpenAI's own filing, which the company has signaled for Q1 2027.

For learners: an IPO book oversubscribed at six to seven times is not normal. In most cycles, three to four times coverage counts as a hot deal. What you are watching in real time is the public market deciding whether frontier-AI valuations are a bubble or the new baseline. Either way, Thursday's open print is the clearest single data point the AI industry will produce this year.
